examples.text: Он говорил, что в номере очень жарко, можно утку пожарить.
examples.trans: He said that it is so hot in the room you could roast a duck.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'maybe', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Папа, может, мне еще его номер обыскать?
examples.trans: Dad, maybe I should search his room too?

examples.text: Денис, можно тебя на минутку?
examples.trans: Denis, may I have a word with you for a minute?

examples.text: Он говорил, что в номере очень жарко, можно утку пожарить.
examples.trans: He said that it is so hot in the room you could roast a duck.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'still', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя есть ещё.
examples.trans: You've still got some.

examples.text: Ты ещё пожалеешь!
examples.trans: You'll be sorry!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ыскать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to search'.

examples.text: Папа, может, мне еще его номер обыскать?
examples.trans: Dad, maybe I should search his room too?

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и обыскать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to search on time.

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'говорить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'talk', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.text: Просто поговори с ним по-дружески.
examples.trans: Just talk with him in a friendly way.

examples.text: Поговори с ним.
examples.trans: Talk to him.

examples.text: Нам надо поговорить.
examples.trans: We need to talk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with / from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Всем спасибо, урок окончен.
examples.trans: Thank you everyone, the session is over.

examples.text: Исследования показали, что день надо начинать с классической музыки.
examples.trans: Studies showed that the day should start with classical music.

examples.text: Тогда производительность труда увеличивается.
examples.trans: Then labor productivity increases.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem '-дружески').

examples.text: Просто поговори с ним по-дружески.
examples.trans: Just talk with him in a friendly way.

examples.text: Костя сказал это совершенно по-дружески и спокойно.
examples.trans: Kostya said this quite in a friendly way and calmly.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'our, ours', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это наш шанс получить звезду!
examples.trans: This is our chance to get a star!

examples.text: Ты помнишь нашего старого профессора?
examples.trans: Do you remember our old professor?

examples.text: Папа, я очень рада, что вы нашли то, что вас объединяет.
examples.trans: Dad, I am very glad that you two found something that unites you.
